Resolves #21475

A `dragResortable` tree list now moves its items by drag. The upper or lower half of a leaf puts the item before or after it, and the middle of a folder takes it in as its last child. While the drag runs, the slot shows on that item as a line or an outline. A drop writes the record's `parentId` and its store position, and the tree renders from the store. A folder never moves into its own subtree. Until now no drag started at all: the zones gated on `draggable`, which a `dragResortable` tree never sets.

Evidence: L3 (component spec with real pointer drags and a unit spec, both in CI; frames released and changed) → L3 required (AC-1..AC-4). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/component/tree/DragMove.spec.mjs` › AC-1, into an open and a closed folder; `test/playwright/unit/draggable/tree/SortZone.spec.mjs` › a leaf moves into a folder as its last child |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `DragMove.spec.mjs` › AC-2, before an item of another folder and after one of its own |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `DragMove.spec.mjs` › AC-3, no slot over the own subtree and the tree unchanged; unit › a folder never moves into itself or its subtree |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `DragMove.spec.mjs` runs every arm with real pointer drags, and its AC-4 arm drags an item out of a `draggable: true` tree |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The seam the ticket did not name.** Every drag guard read `owner.draggable`, so the sort zone of a `dragResortable` tree never received a drag. `Neo.draggable.list.DragZone#isDragEnabled()` replaces the three guards (list drag zone, list sort zone, tree drag zone), and `tree.SortZone` answers it with `dragResortable`.
- **A re-render keeps the drag handle and the open folders.** `tree.List#createItem` marks a draggable item itself; before, only the zone's pass at store load did, so an item rendered later lost its handle. `#setFolderOpen` writes `collapsed` to the record for every caller (`expandAll`, `collapseAll`, `expandParents`, `filter`), replacing the click handler's own copy of that write. Without it, the render after a drop would close every folder "expand all" had opened. `test/playwright/unit/tree/ListRaceCondition.spec.mjs` built its record/VDOM mismatch on `expandParents` not writing the record; it now collapses the record itself and still checks the LI/UL separation it was written for.
- **The proxy.** Open folders stick at z-index 10000 and up, above the proxy's 1000, so the proxy vanished under them; a tree's proxy now sits at 20000, for `draggable` trees too. The sort proxy shrinks to the item's label and floats as a shadowed badge below and to the right of the pointer, clear of the item the pointer is over (operator report, 19 Nov: at the grab point it hid a target folder's label and cut its outline). It may pass the tree's edge (`allowOverdrag`), since the main thread clamps by the item's full width and would push it back over the items. A folder taking an item in is tinted as well as outlined.
- **Out of scope at intake:** opening a closed folder while a drag hovers it. A drop onto a closed folder already moves the item into it.

## Test Evidence

Released (`dev`): a pointer drag from `a.txt` over the folder `sub`. Nothing starts.

<img src="https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/909b8d241a9a28b4fc31d3862e0a5f19431ba126/review-evidence/21475/tree-drag-released-inside.png?raw=true" width="300" alt="dev: the drag starts nothing">

Changed, the same drag: `sub` is tinted and outlined in full with its label in view, the source stays dimmed in place, and the proxy floats below and to the right of the pointer. Then a drag over the upper half of `b.txt` draws the line above it, and the first drop has put `a.txt` into `sub`.

<img src="https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cb972d4273da81ccdc0f32f275e935f40cb154b/review-evidence/21475/tree-drag-v2-inside.png?raw=true" width="300" alt="head: the folder takes the item in, the proxy clear of it"> <img src="https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cb972d4273da81ccdc0f32f275e935f40cb154b/review-evidence/21475/tree-drag-v2-before.png?raw=true" width="300" alt="head: a line above b.txt"> <img src="https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cb972d4273da81ccdc0f32f275e935f40cb154b/review-evidence/21475/tree-drag-v2-dropped.png?raw=true" width="300" alt="head: a.txt inside sub">

What each frame could be faulted for, checked before posting: the target's outline runs unbroken on all four sides, its label reads, and the proxy overlaps no label in either drag frame. The earlier frames at `909b8d241a` had the proxy at the grab point, over the target's label and the left part of its outline.

Red-first in a separate `dev` worktree: the component spec fails 4 of 5 there (no drag starts) and passes only the `draggable: true` arm; 5 of 5 on the head. The AC-1 arm also pins that the proxy covers no part of the target folder; it fails on `1b4ed7e67e` (proxy top at 114 px, folder bottom at 152 px). Full unit suite on the head: 8,133 passed. A throwaway probe spec took the frames; it is not committed.
